heard: Our closest stellar neighbor is completely invisible to the naked eye. Located in the southern constellation Centaurus, Proxima Centauri is a small, low-mass red dwarf star. It has a mass that is only about 10% of the sun's mass. The star's interior is fully convective, meaning it will shine for trillions of years. Yet this quiet fuel burning hides a violent flare star erupting with sudden increases in brightness. It hosts Proxima Centauri b, an Earth-sized exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone every 11.2 Earth days. Intense stellar flares threat to strip away this nearby planet's atmosphere entirely. Ferocious stellar activity is why our closest stellar neighbor is completely invisible to the naked eye.
